precepts.text: But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God. Christ is the wisdom of God. So if any man be in Christ he is a new creature, because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.
precepts.point: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. Reprove with equity means you are not partial. So having the spirit of the Lord, you are not going to be in partiality. You are going to have knowledge and understanding. You are going to obtain, you are going to retain, and you are going to apply. And it shows you the power he will have as well.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

precepts.text: He shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide.
precepts.point: Understand this: all Judah is not in North America, just like all Levi is not on the island of Haiti, and all Benjamin is not on Jamaica or Trinidad. Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide; Zechariah is pointing out a remnant of Judah that is in North America. And what is so special about this group here? The house of David is here. You are going to find that thing out.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
People will hear us teaching and say, oh, you're saying all Judah is in North America. No, that's not what we're saying, just like we know all Levi is not on the island of Haiti, and all Benjamin is not on the island of Jamaica or Trinidad. “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide.

Zechariah is pointing out a remnant of Judah that is in North America. And what's so special about this group here? The house of David is here. You are going to find that thing out.

Why are they so hard on Judah here as opposed to Judah scattered elsewhere? The civil rights hearings of 1959 before the Senate, under the title American Negro problems, say it: the Negro question in the United States of America must be treated in its relation to the huge Negro masses oppressed and exploited by white imperialism in Africa and South America, and the Negroes of the United States are the most advanced section of the Negro population of the world and can play a decisive role in helping and leading the liberation movement of the Negro colonies. You have Negroes in Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Saudi Arabia; Judah is everywhere, the southern kingdom is everywhere. But the white man examined all the Negro populations and said the American Negro is the most advanced.

Deacon Malachi brought it out: when Nebuchadnezzar came against Judah, they took the best of the best, the most educated. Esau isn't stupid; he knows that history. At Elmina Castle in Ghana, the tour guide said it himself: you never ask why the American black is more advanced; when they came to Africa, they took the best of them. Look right after slavery, without even reparations, how the blacks here advanced, and how they came and dropped bombs and destroyed them. That's why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks: that group here is more dangerous than all the other groups where the blacks are. And that's why the Lord said, “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first.” It isn't Judah over in Africa or in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here. This history you should be proud of.

precepts.text: But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them. We shall lay our hands upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon, the Japanese, shall obey us.
precepts.point: Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; over Philistia will I triumph. God says Moab is going to serve.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; over Philistia will I triumph.” God says Moab is going to wash our clothes; they will be our laundromat forever. And he casts his shoe over Edom. That is why we are not supposed to be married to them. God says come out from among them and be ye separate. Some of us come of mixed parentage, and that is fine, but find yourself an Israelite woman, an Israelite man, and don't do this no more.

Isaiah shows the same triumph: “But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together.” We shall fly upon the shoulders of the Palestinians toward the west, and we shall spoil them of the east together.

“they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.” We shall lay our hands upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon, the Japanese, shall obey us.

So the nations that rule over Israel now, Edom, Moab and Ammon, will be under Israel's hand. That is what God means when he calls Moab his washpot and casts his shoe over Edom: they will serve.

precepts.text: That root of Jesse is Christ; to it shall the Gentiles seek. The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, from Assyria (modern day Turkey), from Egypt, from Pathros (Sudan), from Cush (Ethiopia), from Elam (Persia), from Shinar (Iraq), from Hamath (Syria), and from the islands of the sea. He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord's people. The envy also of Ephraim shall depart: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. That is dealing with the hatred between our people; if they want salvation, it does not matter how much they do not like each other.
precepts.point: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was laboring for; that is why he was getting afflicted.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Here is a follow-up, in case Matthew is not good enough for you. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” That root of Jesse is Christ. To it shall the Gentiles seek. So the subject is Gentiles, and we want to see who these Gentiles are.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord’s people, recovered “from Assyria”, that is modern day Turkey; “and from Egypt, and from Pathros”, that is Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Persia; “and from Shinar”, Iraq; “and from Hamath”, Syria; “and from the islands of the sea.”

Then it gets more specific: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” These Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah.

Now, you might be saying, but blacks and Latinos don’t get along too much. Read the next verse: “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” That is dealing with the hatred between our people. If they want salvation, it does not matter how much they don’t like each other in California. God don’t give a damn.

So the “mystery among the Gentiles” in Colossians 1:27 is Christ, the root of Jesse, gathering the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah back together, and ending the envy between them.

precepts.text: The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. How are these people going to rise out of these places if they are never told? They ridicule us for going to Africa, India, Australia, Papua New Guinea; but the people have been scattered to the four corners, and you err, not knowing the scriptures. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street? Where would we be today if this truth never left the streets of Harlem and Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are.
precepts.point: Ye are the light of the world. The scriptures tell us this is a global mission, worldwide. We have to have our aspirations and goals set to a global standard, not a local one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Our people are the remnant, scattered to the four corners of the world.

How are these people going to be able to rise out of these places if they were never told? That is why this gospel has to have a global standard, preached to the whole world. If your leadership ain't talking about covering the earth, they're not the guys. Don't waste your time.

They ridicule us now: y'all going over there to Africa, y'all in India, you went to Australia, you went to Papua New Guinea. We don't give a damn how anybody feels about it. Negro, you do lack the understanding of this Bible; you do err, not knowing the scriptures. The people have been scattered to the four corners. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street, if you want to be known for Times Square or a street corner?

Where would we be today if this truth had stayed in Harlem, if it never left the streets of Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are. Being the light of the world means going where the remnant was scattered, to the islands of the sea, and telling them who they are.

precepts.text: The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. Has this happened yet? No, we are waiting on this second coming. This is why unification is so important: we got to go back to all these places, because our people are there. He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel: those that were kept afar off, living amongst the other nations. The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. All that division, light skin against dark skin, northern kingdom looking at us and us looking at them, is going to be gone. We have all been through changes and look different today, but we are all the same people.
precepts.point: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; in whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord. Right now in this room we got northern and southern kingdom back together again. That wall of partition is done.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what the “middle wall of partition” of Ephesians 2:14 looks like: the hatred, the enmity, the envy and the vexation between the two kingdoms.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Has this happened yet? No. We are waiting on this second coming, waiting to be delivered again. That is why unification is so important: we have to go back to all these places, because our people are there. The Bible says they are in Assyria, in Egypt, in Pathros, in Cush, in Elam, and in the islands of the sea. We have a lot of work to do.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts are those who were kept afar off, living amongst the other nations as heathens, like Hellenized Jews. These are the ones Paul calls those “who sometimes were far off” and are now “made nigh by the blood of Christ.”

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” The envy of Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the wall of partition, and it is going to be gone. No more division: light skinned against dark skinned, look at your hair, look at my hair; the northern kingdom looking at us and us looking at them. Yes, Esau touched the northern kingdom; the southern kingdom has been through changes too. We look different today, but we are all the same people.

That wall is what Christ tore down. “He is our peace, who hath made both one”: the two sticks, Judah and Ephraim, made one, and right now in the congregation northern and southern kingdom are back together again.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Northern kingdom and southern kingdom must apply this law if they want salvation.
precepts.point: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. Whatever the northern kingdom has against the southern kingdom must depart.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart”: whatever the northern kingdom has against the southern kingdom must depart. “Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” Why? Because the Lord’s law requires it. Northern kingdom and southern kingdom must apply this law if they want salvation.

“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. That is it right there. No hatred in the heart, no vengeance, no grudge against the children of your own people.

Instead, “thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.” No one is getting into the kingdom with hatred in their heart. No one is entering New Jerusalem, and you are not making it out of the wilderness, with hatred in your heart.

So Isaiah 11:13 is the law of Leviticus 19 fulfilled among the tribes: the envy between Ephraim and Judah, between the blacks and the Latinos, has to depart. That is why the prophets go out to places like Detroit, where northern kingdom and southern kingdom are heavily segregated, to bring our people together with the word of God in unity and nationhood.

precepts.text: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. When it says thy neighbour, like we read in Leviticus, it means the children of thy people: your own nation. That's something we have not learned; you look at South Africa and they have not learned it either, despising their own people. God's laws must continue to be pushed and taught in this earth. No one is entering New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.
precepts.point: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. Whatever the northern kingdom has against the southern kingdom must depart.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“Master, which is the great commandment in the law? Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

When it says your neighbour, like we read in Leviticus 19:18, it means “the children of thy people.” That is your race. It is literally saying, love your race.

And that is something we have not learned. Look at South Africa: they have not learned it. They love the white man more than their own brother and sister that look just like them, and they despise their own people.

So God’s laws must continue to be pushed and taught in this earth. Ephraim will stop envying Judah, and Judah will stop vexing Ephraim, only when the tribes keep the second great commandment and love the children of their own people as themselves. No one is entering New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.

precepts.text: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: that Branch is Christ; you can read that in Zechariah 6. He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes: the same exact thing he said in John 5:30. So what did God send him to do?
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The Old Testament shows who was sent and why. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: that Branch is Christ, as Zechariah 6 shows. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.”

Then: “and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” That is the same exact thing Christ said in John 5:30: “as I hear, I judge”, “I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” The Branch out of Jesse does not judge by himself; he does the will of the one who sent him.

So what did God send him to do? Keep reading in the same chapter, and verse 12 tells it: to set up an ensign, assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather the dispersed of Judah. When Christ spoke in the New Testament, he was reiterating what the Old Testament already said, and the text substantiates it.

precepts.text: To it shall the Gentiles seek. Who are the Gentiles in this regard? A brother answered: stay in the passage; verses 11 and 12 explain it. The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, and he shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. The Gentiles he is talking about are the outcasts of Israel. That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” Who are the Gentiles here? The Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The answer is Israel, and it is proven by staying in the passage.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The Gentiles that seek the root of Jesse are the outcasts of Israel, the remnant of his people.

That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The Pharisees and chief priests were studied men. They understood this prophecy of the dispersed, which is why they asked whether he would go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles.

precepts.text: The four corners: he shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. It was Israel scattered through the four corners of the earth, living as beasts.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The vessel in Peter's vision was “knit at the four corners.” The four corners are in the prophets too: “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

So what is in that sheet, gathered at the four corners? It was Israel, scattered through the four corners of the earth, living as beasts. The outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah are the ones God assembles from those four corners.

He sets up an ensign “for the nations” because Israel would be scattered among all the nations and live as Gentiles. The picture of a sheet knit at four corners is the picture of God drawing his scattered people together from every end of the earth, and that is the vision Peter had to explain to those of the circumcision.

precepts.text: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse: count the seven upon him. The spirit of the Lord, wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord: the seven pillars, complete spiritual perfection, which is what Christ operated in.
precepts.point: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars. Seven pillars: complete wisdom.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Let's see who this wisdom pertains to and who had these seven pillars. Isaiah: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That is talking about Christ.

Now count what rests upon him. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: that's one. “the spirit of wisdom”: two. “and understanding”: three. “the spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “the spirit of knowledge”: six. “and of the fear of the Lord”: seven.

Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had. Seven represents completion, so they represent complete spiritual perfection, and that is what Christ operated in. Wisdom's house on seven pillars is Christ, full of the spirit of the Lord in every part.

precepts.text: The Lord sets his hand the second time, the first being under Moses, to recover the remnant from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea, and gathers the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: These are they which came out of great tribulation and washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb: so much for not going through tribulation.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” We are the outcasts of Israel.

That is the all nations right there: the remnant of Israel gathered out of every land they were scattered to, the great multitude of Revelation 7:9.

precepts.text: The remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Just in case Isaiah 27 is not enough, beat a dead horse. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” That is the same gathering we read in Isaiah 27.

From where? “Which shall be left, from Assyria”: my people. “And from Egypt”: Egypt, my people. “And from Pathros”: still Egypt, my people. “And from Cush, and from Elam”: Elam is Iran and Pakistan, my people. “And from Shinar”: Shinar is Iraq, my people. “And from Hamath”: Syria, my people. “And from the islands of the sea”: the islands, whether the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. That is his people.

It names Assyria and Egypt right there with the rest, and in every one of those places it is the remnant of his people that he recovers, not the nations of those lands. So when Isaiah 19 says “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands”, it is speaking of Israel scattered in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Lord recovers the second time.

precepts.text: He shall assemble the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: What God hath cleansed, call not thou common. As at Hezekiah's Passover, God pardoned and cleansed northern Israelites who sought him, and the vision has nothing to do with eating pork.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
The sheet Peter saw was “knit at the four corners”, and Isaiah shows why: “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.”

The nations here are Israel. He will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather the dispersed of Judah, as Hosea said, from the four corners of the earth. A vessel knit at the four corners: that is Israel scattered to every corner, and the Lord gathering them.

That is what the vision meant. Peter doubted in himself what it should mean, thinking what Christians think, that he was told to eat unclean food. But he saw it three times, and three men came from Cornelius. Then he understood: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” The vision was about a man, Cornelius, one of the outcasts of Israel from the northern kingdom whom Judah called common and unclean.

What God hath cleansed, call not thou common: the Lord is gathering both houses, the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah, and making them clean, one nation again, as Ezekiel said, “neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

“the lion shall eat straw like the ox”, the sucking child plays on the hole of the asp, and “They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.” The original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

That is the pattern of running to a nation that cannot save, the same spirit that trusts in the systems of the world instead of the Most High.
